newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China grain consumption to outstrip output.
newsitem.headline: China grain consumption to outstrip output.

text.p: Chinese grain consumption will reach 690.8 million tonnes against production of 646.9 million tonnes in the year 2020, an official of China's National Rice Research Institute said on Friday.
"It can be expected that grain imports will be needed to compensate for...demand, but massive amount of imports will not be needed," Qiu Ling Cang told an Asia rice conference in Singapore.
He said lower grain consumption caused by increased urbanisation and changes in peoples' eating habits will help trim grain consumption.
Most of the increase in consumption will be caused by increasing amounts of grain being used as animal feed.
"Feed for livestock has become the largest portion of grain consumed in China entering the 21st century," Qiu said.

Production in 2000 will probably reach 494.9 million tonnes against consumption estimated at 527.4 million. In 2010, output will rise to 570.9 million tonnes but consumption will reach 614.2 million tonnes.
